#!/usr/bin/env python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Modern climate data analysis.

Python 3 port of the legacy ``climate_analyzer/analyze_climate.py`` script.
Reads station temperatures from a UTF-8 CSV, reports mean temperature per
station, and can plot temperature anomalies.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import configparser
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DEFAULT_CONFIG = BASE_DIR / "climate_analyzer" / "config.ini"
DEFAULT_DATA = BASE_DIR / "climate_analyzer" / "sample_data" / "climate_data.csv"


class ClimateAnalyzer:
    """Load climate observations and compute per-station statistics."""

    def __init__(self, config_path: Path | None = None) -> None:
        self.config_path = Path(config_path) if config_path else DEFAULT_CONFIG
        self.config = configparser.ConfigParser()
        # ``read`` is silent on a missing file, which keeps the analyzer usable
        # without a config; callers can check ``self.config.sections()``.
        self.config.read(self.config_path, encoding="utf-8")
        self.data_cache: dict[str, pd.DataFrame] = {}

    def load_temperature_data(self, filename: Path | str) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Load the CSV as UTF-8 and parse the date column on Python 3."""
        path = Path(filename)
        df = pd.read_csv(
            path,
            encoding="utf-8",
            parse_dates=["date"],
            date_format="%Y-%m-%d",
        )

        required = {"date", "station_id", "station_name", "temperature"}
        missing = required - set(df.columns)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{path} is missing required column(s): {', '.join(sorted(missing))}"
            )

        # CSVs are decoded as text already, so there is no ``unicode(x, ...)``
        # call to make; stripping only guards against stray padding.
        df["station_name"] = df["station_name"].astype(str).str.strip()
        df["temperature"] = pd.to_numeric(df["temperature"], errors="coerce")
        df = df.dropna(subset=["temperature"]).reset_index(drop=True)

        self.data_cache[str(path)] = df
        return df

    @staticmethod
    def calculate_anomalies(temperature_series: pd.Series) -> np.ndarray:
        """Return each observation's departure from the series mean."""
        values = temperature_series.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)
        if values.size == 0:
            return np.array([], dtype=np.float64)
        return values - np.mean(values, dtype=np.float64)

    def mean_temperatures(self, data: pd.DataFrame) -> dict[int, float]:
        """Map each station id to its mean temperature."""
        means = data.groupby("station_id", sort=True)["temperature"].mean()
        return {int(station): float(value) for station, value in means.items()}

    def create_visualization(
        self,
        data: pd.Series,
        title: str,
        output_path: Path | str | None = None,
    ) -> Path:
        """Save a time-series plot of ``data`` and return the output path."""
        # Imported lazily so the numeric analysis works without matplotlib and
        # so a headless backend is selected before pyplot is initialised.
        import matplotlib

        matplotlib.use("Agg")
        import matplotlib.dates as mdates
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

        width = self.config.getint("plotting", "figure_width", fallback=12)
        height = self.config.getint("plotting", "figure_height", fallback=8)
        dpi = self.config.getint("plotting", "dpi", fallback=300)

        target = Path(output_path) if output_path else Path("/tmp/climate_plot.png")

        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(width, height))
        ax.plot(data.index, data.to_numpy(), color="tab:blue", linewidth=1.2)
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=16, fontweight="bold")
        ax.set_xlabel("Date")
        ax.set_ylabel("Temperature anomaly (°C)")
        ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mdates.DateFormatter("%Y-%m"))
        ax.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.AutoDateLocator())
        fig.autofmt_xdate()
        fig.tight_layout()
        fig.savefig(target, dpi=dpi)
        plt.close(fig)
        return target

    def run_analysis(
        self,
        data_path: Path | str | None = None,
        plot: bool = False,
    ) -> dict[int, float]:
        """Run the analysis pipeline and return per-station mean temperatures."""
        path = Path(data_path) if data_path else DEFAULT_DATA
        print("Starting climate analysis...")

        data = self.load_temperature_data(path)
        results = self.mean_temperatures(data)

        for station_id, mean_temp in results.items():
            print(f"Station {station_id} mean temperature: {mean_temp:.1f}°C")

        if plot:
            output_path = self.config.get(
                "analysis", "output_path", fallback="/tmp/climate_results"
            )
            plot_path = Path(f"{output_path}.png")
            for station_id in results:
                group = data[data["station_id"] == station_id].sort_values("date")
                anomalies = self.calculate_anomalies(group["temperature"])
                series = pd.Series(anomalies, index=group["date"])
                self.create_visualization(
                    series,
                    f"Temperature Anomalies - Station {station_id}",
                    plot_path.with_name(f"{plot_path.stem}_station_{station_id}.png"),
                )

        print("Analysis completed successfully!")
        return results


def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--data",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_DATA,
        help=f"CSV file to analyse (default: {DEFAULT_DATA})",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        default=DEFAULT_CONFIG,
        help=f"configuration file (default: {DEFAULT_CONFIG})",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--plot",
        action="store_true",
        help="also write anomaly plots for each station",
    )
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)
    try:
        analyzer = ClimateAnalyzer(args.config)
        analyzer.run_analysis(args.data, plot=args.plot)
    except (OSError, ValueError, configparser.Error) as exc:
        print(f"Error occurred: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
PYEOF
